english.title: Fail to report transaction under visitor's shotgun permit
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having

(A)_[sold]_
(B)_[let on hire]_
(C)_[given]_
(D)_[lent]_

a shotgun with a magazine to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) who showed that

(E)_[he]_
(F)_[she]_

was entitled to purchase or acquire the weapon as the holder of a Visitor's Shotgun Permit under section 17 of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1988 but who failed to show that the purchase or acquisition fell within section 17(1A)(c) or section 17(1A)(d) of the Firearms (Amendment) Act 1988 or that

(G)_[he]_
(H)_[she]_

then resided outside Great Britain, failed to comply with section 42A(1) of the Firearms Act 1968 in that you did not, within 48 hours of the transaction, send by registered post or the recorded delivery service notice of the transaction to the chief officer of police for **(..SPECIFY FORCE..) who had granted that permit.
english.legislation: Contrary to section 42A(3) of and Schedule 6 to the Firearms Act 1968.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See also the associated offence wording H4420 re failure to comply with section 42A(2).
(ii) Section 42A(2) lists the matters to be contained in a notice.

other.penalty:
Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
